question: The SI unit of power of a lens is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**dioptre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SI unit of the power of a lens is the **dioptre** (D).
 
• One dioptre is equivalent to the power of a lens with a focal length of one meter.
 
• The power of a lens (P) is given by the formula **P = 1/f**, where f is the focal length in meters.
 
• A positive dioptre value indicates a converging lens, while a negative value indicates a diverging lens.
 
• Dioptres are commonly used by optometrists and ophthalmologists to prescribe corrective lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lens Formula:** The lens formula is given by **1/f = (n-1) * [1/R1 - 1/R2]**, where n is the refractive index of the lens material, and R1 and R2 are the radii of curvature of the two surfaces of the lens.
 
• **Converging and Diverging Lenses:** Converging lenses (convex) have positive focal lengths, while diverging lenses (concave) have negative focal lengths.
 
• **Focal Length:** The focal length of a lens is the distance from the lens to the point where parallel rays of light converge (or appear to diverge from) after passing through the lens.
 
• **Optical Power:** Optical power is a measure of how much a lens converges or diverges light. It is an important parameter in designing optical systems.
 
• **Prescription Lenses:** The power of prescription lenses is specified in dioptres. For example, a prescription of -2.0 D indicates a lens with a focal length of -0.5 meters.
